summary: The harness/server protocol is still too underspecified to serve as a stable implementation target.
detail: FEAT-0008 says the server speaks JSON-RPC with bidirectional streaming and lists message names, but it does not define request/stream correlation, cancellation, stream lifecycle, capability negotiation, protocol versioning, or how tool schemas become visible to the server and model. FEAT-0009, FEAT-0010, and FEAT-0012 all depend on this contract. Without a concrete protocol spec, the feature is still describing intent rather than a stable behavior target.
recommendation: Add a protocol appendix or linked ADR that specifies framing, correlation IDs, stream ownership, cancellation, capability/tool registration, auth handshake boundaries, and version negotiation before this feature is accepted.

summary: The feature changes the provider adapter contract without an explicit ADR update.
detail: ADR-0006 is framed around provider detection, parsing, usage extraction, and stream reassembly. FEAT-0008 extends that contract to outbound formatting and full-history translation across multiple provider message shapes. That is a sensible direction, but it materially changes a constraining interface and should not stay implicit inside the feature spec.
recommendation: Amend or supersede ADR-0006 to define the expanded provider interface explicitly, then keep FEAT-0008 focused on the user-visible server behavior that depends on that interface.

summary: The spec promises new session- and turn-level reporting behavior without defining the storage contract behind it.
detail: The feature promises per-turn cost updates, per-session totals, model-switch history, session inspection commands, and future concurrent harness support. ADR-0007 only establishes hourly and daily provider/model aggregates, and FEAT-0008 does not define the new tables or retention semantics for session and turn data. That leaves a gap between the proposed CLI behavior and the storage contract needed to support it.
recommendation: Add the minimal session/turn persistence model to this feature, or split the storage/reporting portion into a smaller supporting patch or ADR so the acceptance target is concrete.
